sanskrit: atha saṃsmārayām āsa rāghavaṃ mātalis tadā ajānann iva kiṃ vīra tvam enam anuvartase
english: Then Mātali reminded Rāghava at that moment, saying as if in ignorance: 'O hero, why do you keep following him?'

sanskrit: visṛjāsmai vadhāya tvam astraṃ paitāmahaṃ prabho vināśakālaḥ kathito yaḥ suraiḥ so 'dya vartate
english: 'Release upon him, O lord, the weapon descended from Brahmā for his destruction — the hour of his annihilation that was foretold by the gods is now at hand.'

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃsmārito rāmas tena vākyena mātaleḥ jagrāha sa śaraṃ dīptaṃ niśvasantam ivoragam
english: Then Rāma, reminded by those words of Mātali, took up that blazing arrow that hissed like a serpent.

sanskrit: yam asmai prathamaṃ prādād agastyo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ brahmadattaṃ mahad bāṇam amoghaṃ yudhi vīryavān
english: That great, infallible arrow, bestowed by Brahmā and given first to him by the revered sage Agastya the mighty — that arrow which never misses in battle —

sanskrit: brahmaṇā nirmitaṃ pūrvam indrārtham amitaujasā dattaṃ surapateḥ pūrvaṃ trilokajayakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: — had been fashioned of old by Brahmā of boundless might for Indra's sake, and given formerly to the lord of gods who desired the conquest of the three worlds.

sanskrit: yasya vājeṣu pavanaḥ phale pāvakabhāskarau śarīram ākāśamayaṃ gaurave merumandarau
english: In its feathers dwells the wind-god, in its tip fire and the sun; its body is made of sky, and in weight it equals Meru and Mandara.

sanskrit: jājvalyamānaṃ vapuṣā supuṅkhaṃ hemabhūṣitam tejasā sarvabhūtānāṃ kṛtaṃ bhāskaravarcasaṃ
english: Blazing in its form, beautifully fletched, adorned with gold, it was made with the radiance of all living beings and shone with the brilliance of the sun.

sanskrit: sadhūmam iva kālāgniṃ dīptam āśīviṣaṃ yathā rathanāgāśvavṛndānāṃ bhedanaṃ kṣiprakāriṇam
english: Like the fire of universal dissolution with its smoke, like a blazing venomous serpent, swift in action, it could cleave through hosts of chariots, elephants, and horses.

sanskrit: dvārāṇāṃ parighāṇāṃ ca girīṇām api bhedanam nānārudhirasiktāṅgaṃ medodigdhaṃ sudāruṇam
english: It could break through gates and iron bars and even mountains; dreadful, smeared with fat, its body sprinkled with many kinds of blood.

sanskrit: vajrasāraṃ mahānādaṃ nānāsamitidāruṇam sarvavitrāsanaṃ bhīmaṃ śvasantam iva pannagam
english: Hard as a thunderbolt, roaring mightily, fearsome in many battles, terrifying to all, dreadful, hissing like a snake.

sanskrit: kaṅkagṛdhrabalānāṃ ca gomāyugaṇarakṣasām nityaṃ bhakṣapradaṃ yuddhe yamarūpaṃ bhayāvaham
english: In battle it was ever a feast for flocks of herons, vultures, jackals, and rākṣasas; bearing the form of Yama, inspiring dread.

sanskrit: nandanaṃ vānarendrāṇāṃ rakṣasām avasādanam vājitaṃ vividhair vājaiś cārucitrair garutmataḥ
english: A delight to the monkey-lords, a destroyer of rākṣasas, it was feathered with the manifold, beautifully variegated plumes of Garuḍa.

sanskrit: tam uttameṣuṃ lokānām ikṣvākubhayanāśanam dviṣatāṃ kīrtiharaṇaṃ praharṣakaram ātmanaḥ
english: That supreme arrow of the worlds, destroyer of the fears of the Ikṣvāku line, stripping the glory from enemies, filling himself with joy —

sanskrit: abhimantrya tato rāmas taṃ maheṣuṃ mahābalaḥ vedaproktena vidhinā saṃdadhe kārmuke balī
english: — the mighty, powerful Rāma consecrated that great arrow with the rite prescribed by Vedic injunction and fitted it to his bow.

sanskrit: sa rāvaṇāya saṃkruddho bhṛśam āyamya kārmukam cikṣepa param āyattas taṃ śaraṃ marmaghātinam
english: Deeply enraged at Rāvaṇa, he drew the bow fully taut and released that arrow that strikes the vital points, exerting his utmost force.

sanskrit: sa vajra iva durdharṣo vajrabāhuvisarjitaḥ kṛtānta iva cāvāryo nyapatad rāvaṇorasi
english: Irresistible as the thunderbolt hurled from Indra's arm, unstoppable as Fate itself, it fell upon Rāvaṇa's chest.

sanskrit: sa visṛṣṭo mahāvegaḥ śarīrāntakaraḥ śaraḥ bibheda hṛdayaṃ tasya rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
english: Released with tremendous velocity, that body-ending arrow pierced the heart of the evil-souled Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: rudhirāktaḥ sa vegena jīvitāntakaraḥ śaraḥ rāvaṇasya haran prāṇān viveśa dharaṇītalam
english: Blood-smeared, that life-ending arrow, bearing away Rāvaṇa's vital breath with its speed, entered into the earth.

sanskrit: sa śaro rāvaṇaṃ hatvā rudhirārdrakṛtacchaviḥ kṛtakarmā nibhṛtavat svatūṇīṃ punar āviśat
english: That arrow, having slain Rāvaṇa, its surface wet with blood, its task accomplished, quietly returned to its own quiver.

sanskrit: tasya hastād dhatasyāśu kārmukaṃ tat sasāyakam nipapāta saha prāṇair bhraśyamānasya jīvitāt
english: From the hand of the struck one, the bow with its arrow fell quickly to the ground along with his life-breath as it departed from him.

sanskrit: gatāsur bhīmavegas tu nairṛtendro mahādyutiḥ papāta syandanād bhūmau vṛtro vajrahato yathā
english: His life-breath gone, the lord of the rākṣasas of terrific speed and great splendor fell from his chariot to the ground, like Vṛtra struck by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā patitaṃ bhūmau hataśeṣā niśācarāḥ hatanāthā bhayatrastāḥ sarvataḥ saṃpradudruvuḥ
english: Seeing him fallen to the ground, the surviving night-roamers, bereft of their master and trembling with fear, fled in all directions.

sanskrit: nardantaś cābhipetus tān vānarā drumayodhinaḥ daśagrīvavadhaṃ dṛṣṭvā vijayaṃ rāghavasya ca
english: The tree-fighting monkeys, roaring, fell upon them, having witnessed the slaying of the ten-necked one and Rāghava's victory.

sanskrit: arditā vānarair hṛṣṭair laṅkām abhyapatan bhayāt hatāśrayatvāt karuṇair bāṣpaprasravaṇair mukhaiḥ
english: Tormented by the exultant monkeys, the rākṣasas fled in fear toward Laṅkā, their refuge destroyed, their faces pitiful, streaming with tears.

sanskrit: tato vineduḥ saṃhṛṣṭā vānarā jitakāśinaḥ vadanto rāghavajayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca taṃ vadham
english: Then the joyful monkeys, wearing the look of conquerors, let out a great cry, proclaiming Rāghava's victory and the death of Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: athāntarikṣe vyanadat saumyas tridaśadundubhiḥ divyagandhavahas tatra mārutaḥ susukho vavau
english: Then the auspicious divine kettledrums of the gods resounded in the sky, and a sweet breeze bearing celestial fragrances blew there.

sanskrit: nipapātāntarikṣāc ca puṣpavṛṣṭis tadā bhuvi kirantī rāghavarathaṃ duravāpā manoharāḥ
english: And from the sky a rain of flowers fell to the earth, scattering the charming, hard-to-obtain blossoms over Rāghava's chariot.

sanskrit: rāghavastavasaṃyuktā gagane ca viśuśruve sādhu sādhv iti vāg agryā devatānāṃ mahātmanām
english: In the sky, joined with praises of Rāghava, there was heard the excellent speech of the great-souled gods: 'Well done! Well done!'

sanskrit: āviveśa mahān harṣo devānāṃ cāraṇaiḥ saha rāvaṇe nihate raudre sarvalokabhayaṃkare
english: Great joy filled the gods together with the cāraṇas at the slaying of the fierce Rāvaṇa who had been the terror of all the worlds.

sanskrit: tataḥ sakāmaṃ sugrīvam aṅgadaṃ ca mahābalam cakāra rāghavaḥ prīto hatvā rākṣasapuṃgavam
english: Then Rāghava, delighted, having slain the foremost of rākṣasas, fulfilled the wishes of Sugrīva and the mighty Aṅgada.

sanskrit: tataḥ prajagmuḥ praśamaṃ marudgaṇā diśaḥ prasedur vimalaṃ nabho 'bhavat mahī cakampe na ca mārutā vavuḥ sthiraprabhaś cāpy abhavad divākaraḥ
english: Then the wind-hosts grew calm, the directions became clear, the sky became cloudless, the earth did not tremble, the winds ceased to blow, and the sun became steady in its brilliance.

sanskrit: tatas tu sugrīvavibhīṣaṇādayaḥ suhṛdviśeṣāḥ sahalakṣmaṇās tadā sametya hṛṣṭā vijayena rāghavaṃ raṇe 'bhirāmaṃ vidhinābhyapūjayan
english: Then Sugrīva, Vibhīṣaṇa, and the other dear friends, together with Lakṣmaṇa, came together in joy at the victory and honored Rāghava, who was splendid in battle, with due ceremony.

sanskrit: sa tu nihataripuḥ sthirapratijñaḥ svajanabalābhivṛto raṇe rarāja raghukulanṛpanandano mahaujās tridaśagaṇair abhisaṃvṛto yathendraḥ
english: He, the enemy slain, his vow fulfilled, surrounded by the forces of his own people in battle, shone forth — the glorious son of the king of the Raghu line — surrounded by hosts of gods, like Indra himself.

sanskrit: rāvaṇaṃ nihataṃ śrutvā rāghaveṇa mahātmanā antaḥpurād viniṣpetū rākṣasyaḥ śokakarśitāḥ
english: Hearing that Rāvaṇa had been slain by the great-souled Rāghava, the rākṣasī women poured out from the inner apartments, emaciated with grief.

sanskrit: vāryamāṇāḥ subahuśo vṛṣṭantyaḥ kṣitipāṃsuṣu vimuktakeśyo duḥkhārtā gāvo vatsahatā yathā
english: Though restrained again and again, weeping, rolling in the dust of the earth, their hair unbound, agonized with grief — like cows whose calves have been killed.

sanskrit: uttareṇa viniṣkramya dvāreṇa saha rākṣasaiḥ praviśyāyodhanaṃ ghoraṃ vicinvantyo hataṃ patim
english: Going out through the northern gate together with the rākṣasas, they entered the dreadful battlefield, searching for their slain lord.

sanskrit: āryaputreti vādinyo hā nātheti ca sarvaśaḥ paripetuḥ kabandhāṅkāṃ mahīṃ śoṇitakardamām
english: Crying 'O noble son!' and 'Alas, my master!' on every side, they rushed about over the earth thick with headless trunks, mired in blood.

sanskrit: tā bāṣpaparipūrṇākṣyo bhartṛśokaparājitāḥ kareṇva iva nardantyo vinedur hatayūthapāḥ
english: Their eyes filled with tears, overcome by grief for their husband, they cried out like she-elephants whose herd-bull has been slain.

sanskrit: dadṛśus tā mahākāyaṃ mahāvīryaṃ mahādyutim rāvaṇaṃ nihataṃ bhūmau nīlāñjanacayopamam
english: They beheld Rāvaṇa, of massive body, great might, and great splendor, slain upon the ground, resembling a heap of dark collyrium.

sanskrit: tāḥ patiṃ sahasā dṛṣṭvā śayānaṃ raṇapāṃsuṣu nipetus tasya gātreṣu chinnā vanalatā iva
english: Suddenly seeing their husband lying in the dust of the battlefield, they fell upon his limbs like severed forest creepers.

sanskrit: bahumānāt pariṣvajya kā cid enaṃ ruroda ha caraṇau kā cid āliṅgya kā cit kaṇṭhe 'valambya ca
english: Out of reverence one embraced him and wept; another clasped his feet; yet another hung about his neck.

sanskrit: uddhṛtya ca bhujau kā cid bhūmau sma parivartate hatasya vadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā kā cin moham upāgamat
english: One raised his arms and rolled on the ground; another, gazing upon the face of the slain one, fell into a swoon.

sanskrit: kā cid aṅke śiraḥ kṛtvā ruroda mukham īkṣatī snāpayantī mukhaṃ bāṣpais tuṣārair iva paṅkajam
english: One, placing his head in her lap and gazing at his face, wept, bathing his face with tears as with cold dew upon a lotus.

sanskrit: evam ārtāḥ patiṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇaṃ nihataṃ bhuvi cukruśur bahudhā śokād bhūyas tāḥ paryadevayan
english: Thus afflicted, seeing their husband Rāvaṇa slain upon the earth, they cried out repeatedly in many ways and lamented again and again in their grief.

sanskrit: yena vitrāsitaḥ śakro yena vitrāsito yamaḥ yena vaiśravaṇo rājā puṣpakeṇa viyojitaḥ
english: He by whom Śakra was terrified, by whom Yama was terrified, by whom king Vaiśravaṇa was separated from the Puṣpaka —

sanskrit: gandharvāṇām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca surāṇāṃ ca mahātmanām bhayaṃ yena mahad dattaṃ so 'yaṃ śete raṇe hataḥ
english: — he who gave great fear to the gandharvas, the sages, and the great-souled gods — that same one now lies slain in battle.

sanskrit: asurebhyaḥ surebhyo vā pannagebhyo 'pi vā tathā na bhayaṃ yo vijānāti tasyedaṃ mānuṣād bhayam
english: He who knew no fear from asuras, from gods, or even from serpents — for him has come this fear from a human being.

sanskrit: avadhyo devatānāṃ yas tathā dānavarakṣasām hataḥ so 'yaṃ raṇe śete mānuṣeṇa padātinā
english: He who was unkillable by the gods, by dānavas and rākṣasas alike — that same one lies slain in battle by a human fighting on foot.

sanskrit: yo na śakyaḥ surair hantuṃ na yakṣair nāsurais tathā so 'yaṃ kaś cid ivāsattvo mṛtyuṃ martyena lambhitaḥ
english: He who could not be killed by gods, yakṣas, or asuras — this one, as if a trifling thing, has been brought to death by a mortal.

sanskrit: evaṃ vadantyo bahudhā rurudus tasya tāḥ striyaḥ bhūya eva ca duḥkhārtā vilepuś ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Speaking thus in many ways, his women wept; and further overwhelmed with grief, they lamented again and again.

sanskrit: aśṛṇvatā tu suhṛdāṃ satataṃ hitavādinām etāḥ samam idānīṃ te vayam ātmā ca pātitāḥ
english: 'By your not heeding the friends who ever counseled your good, you have now brought down together — these women, us, and yourself.'

sanskrit: bruvāṇo 'pi hitaṃ vākyam iṣṭo bhrātā vibhīṣaṇaḥ dhṛṣṭaṃ paruṣito mohāt tvayātmavadhakāṅkṣiṇā
english: 'Even your dear brother Vibhīṣaṇa, speaking words of benefit, was boldly treated harshly by you in your delusion, you who sought your own destruction.'

sanskrit: yadi niryātitā te syāt sītā rāmāya maithilī na naḥ syād vyasanaṃ ghoram idaṃ mūlaharaṃ mahat
english: 'Had Sītā the Maithilī been restored by you to Rāma, this dreadful, root-destroying great calamity would not have befallen us.'

sanskrit: vṛttakāmo bhaved bhrātā rāmo mitrakulaṃ bhavet vayaṃ cāvidhavāḥ sarvāḥ sakāmā na ca śatravaḥ
english: 'Your brother's wish would have been fulfilled, Rāma would have become a friendly lineage, all of us would remain unwidowed with our desires fulfilled, and the enemies would not have prevailed.'

sanskrit: tvayā punar nṛśaṃsena sītāṃ saṃrundhatā balāt rākṣasā vayam ātmā ca trayaṃ tulaṃ nipātitam
english: 'But by you, cruel one, forcibly detaining Sītā, three have been cast down into one scale — the rākṣasas, ourselves, and you yourself.'

sanskrit: na kāmakāraḥ kāmaṃ vā tava rākṣasapuṃgava daivaṃ ceṣṭayate sarvaṃ hataṃ daivena hanyate
english: 'O foremost of rākṣasas, this was not your free will or your desire — fate drives everything; what is destroyed is destroyed by fate.'

sanskrit: vānarāṇāṃ vināśo 'yaṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca te raṇe tava caiva mahābāho daivayogād upāgataḥ
english: 'O mighty-armed one, this destruction of monkeys and your rākṣasas in battle, and indeed of yourself, has come about through the conjunction of fate.'

sanskrit: naivārthena na kāmena vikrameṇa na cājñayā śakyā daivagatir loke nivartayitum udyatā
english: 'The course of fate, once set in motion, cannot be reversed in this world — not by wealth, not by desire, not by valor, not by command.'

sanskrit: vilepur evaṃ dīnās tā rākṣasādhipayoṣitaḥ kurarya iva duḥkhārtā bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇāḥ
english: Thus those pitiable wives of the lord of rākṣasas lamented, grief-stricken like ospreys, their eyes clouded with tears.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ vilapamānānāṃ tathā rākṣasayoṣitām jyeṣṭhā patnī priyā dīnā bhartāraṃ samudaikṣata
english: Among those lamenting rākṣasī women, his chief and beloved wife, pitiable, gazed upon her husband.

sanskrit: daśagrīvaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmeṇācintyakarmaṇā patiṃ mandodarī tatra kṛpaṇā paryadevayat
english: Seeing the ten-necked one slain by Rāma of inconceivable deeds, Mandodarī there lamented pitiably for her husband.

sanskrit: nanu nāma mahābāho tava vaiśravaṇānuja kruddhasya pramukhe sthātuṃ trasyaty api puraṃdaraḥ
english: 'O mighty-armed one, O younger brother of Vaiśravaṇa — even Purandara trembles to stand before you when you are angered.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś ca mahīdevā gandharvāś ca yaśasvinaḥ nanu nāma tavodvegāc cāraṇāś ca diśo gatāḥ
english: The sages, the earthly gods, the glorious gandharvas, and the cāraṇas — did they not flee to the directions in terror of you?

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ mānuṣamātreṇa rāmeṇa yudhi nirjitaḥ na vyapatrapase rājan kim idaṃ rākṣasarṣabha
english: And yet you, O king, O bull among rākṣasas, are defeated in battle by a mere human named Rāma — are you not ashamed? What is this?

sanskrit: kathaṃ trailokyam ākramya śriyā vīryeṇa cānvitam aviṣahyaṃ jaghāna tvāṃ mānuṣo vanagocaraḥ
english: How did a human who wanders in the forest kill you — who had subjugated the three worlds endowed with glory and valor, you who were invincible?

sanskrit: mānuṣāṇām aviṣaye carataḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ vināśas tava rāmeṇa saṃyuge nopapadyate
english: Your destruction at the hands of Rāma in battle is not fitting for one who roams beyond the reach of humans, who can assume any form at will.

sanskrit: na caitat karma rāmasya śraddadhāmi camūmukhe sarvataḥ samupetasya tava tenābhimarśanam
english: I cannot believe this is Rāma's own doing — that he, facing you in battle, you who were assailed from all sides, should have struck you down.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi purā jitvā jitaṃ tribhuvanaṃ tvayā smaradbhir iva tad vairam indriyair eva nirjitaḥ
english: Having once conquered the senses you conquered the three worlds; now, as if those senses remembered that enmity, you were yourself conquered by the senses.

sanskrit: atha vā rāmarūpeṇa vāsavaḥ svayam āgataḥ māyāṃ tava vināśāya vidhāyāpratitarkitām
english: Or rather, Vāsava himself has come in the form of Rāma, contriving an illusion for your destruction that was beyond reckoning.

sanskrit: yadaiva hi janasthāne rākṣasair bahubhir vṛtaḥ kharas tava hato bhrātā tadaivāsau na mānuṣaḥ
english: The very moment your brother Khara, surrounded by many rākṣasas, was slain at Janasthāna — from that moment alone, he was no human being.

sanskrit: yadaiva nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ duṣpraveṣāṃ surair api praviṣṭo hanumān vīryāt tadaiva vyathitā vayam
english: The very moment Hanūmān by his might entered the city of Laṅkā — difficult of entry even for gods — from that very moment we were distressed.

sanskrit: kriyatām avirodhaś ca rāghaveṇeti yan mayā ucyamāno na gṛhṇāsi tasyeyaṃ vyuṣṭir āgatā
english: 'Let there be no enmity with Rāghava' — so I said to you, and you would not accept it; the consequence of that has now arrived.

sanskrit: akasmāc cābhikāmo 'si sītāṃ rākṣasapuṃgava aiśvaryasya vināśāya dehasya svajanasya ca
english: You conceived an unprovoked desire for Sītā, O foremost of rākṣasas — for the destruction of your sovereignty, your body, and your own people.

sanskrit: arundhatyā viśiṣṭāṃ tāṃ rohiṇyāś cāpi durmate sītāṃ dharṣayatā mānyāṃ tvayā hy asadṛśaṃ kṛtam
english: By violating Sītā, who surpasses even Arundhatī and Rohiṇī, O foolish one, by molesting that venerable woman, you have done what is unbecoming of you.

sanskrit: na kulena na rūpeṇa na dākṣiṇyena maithilī mayādhikā vā tulyā vā tvaṃ tu mohān na budhyase
english: The Maithilī is not superior to me nor even my equal in birth, beauty, or gracious conduct — but you in your delusion did not perceive this.

sanskrit: sarvathā sarvabhūtānāṃ nāsti mṛtyur alakṣaṇaḥ tava tāvad ayaṃ mṛtyur maithilīkṛtalakṣaṇaḥ
english: In every way, no death of any creature is without its mark — and your death, for one, bears the mark made by Maithilī.

sanskrit: maithilī saha rāmeṇa viśokā vihariṣyati alpapuṇyā tv ahaṃ ghore patitā śokasāgare
english: Maithilī will sport with Rāma free of grief, while I, of meager merit, have fallen into a dreadful ocean of sorrow.

sanskrit: kailāse mandare merau tathā caitrarathe vane devodyāneṣu sarveṣu vihṛtya sahitā tvayā
english: Having sported with you on Kailāsa, Mandara, and Meru, and in the Caitraratha forest and all the divine gardens —

sanskrit: vimānenānurūpeṇa yā yāmy atulayā śriyā paśyantī vividhān deśāṃs tāṃs tāṃś citrasragambarā bhraṃśitā kāmabhogebhyaḥ sāsmi vīravadhāt tava
english: — I who used to travel in a fitting aerial car with incomparable splendor, adorned with bright garlands and garments, beholding those various lands — I am cast down from all pleasures of desire by the slaying of you, my hero.

sanskrit: satyavāk sa mahābhāgo devaro me yad abravīt ayaṃ rākṣasamukhyānāṃ vināśaḥ paryupasthitaḥ
english: True indeed were the words spoken by my greatly fortunate brother-in-law: 'The destruction of the foremost rākṣasas is at hand.'

sanskrit: kāmakrodhasamutthena vyasanena prasaṅginā tvayā kṛtam idaṃ sarvam anāthaṃ rakṣasāṃ kulam
english: Through a calamity arising from desire and wrath, through entanglement with vice, you have done this — made the entire lineage of rākṣasas without a protector.

sanskrit: na hi tvaṃ śocitavyo me prakhyātabalapauruṣaḥ strīsvabhāvāt tu me buddhiḥ kāruṇye parivartate
english: You of renowned strength and manhood are not truly to be mourned by me; but by the nature of women my mind turns to compassion.

sanskrit: sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ ca tvaṃ gṛhītvā svāṃ gatiṃ gataḥ ātmānam anuśocāmi tvadviyogena duḥkhitām
english: Taking with you both your good deeds and your evil deeds, you have gone to your own final course; I mourn for myself, who am made wretched by separation from you.

sanskrit: nīlajīmūtasaṃkāśaḥ pītāmbaraśubhāṅgadaḥ sarvagātrāṇi vikṣipya kiṃ śeṣe rudhirāplutaḥ prasupta iva śokārtāṃ kiṃ māṃ na pratibhāṣase
english: Dark as a blue storm-cloud, adorned with bright golden armlets and yellow garments, your limbs flung wide, you lie drenched in blood — as if asleep. Why do you not speak to me who am tormented with grief?

sanskrit: mahāvīryasya dakṣasya saṃyugeṣv apalāyinaḥ yātudhānasya dauhitrīṃ kiṃ tvaṃ māṃ nābhyudīkṣase
english: Why do you not look up at me, the granddaughter of the great-valiant, capable, never-retreating in battle rākṣasa?

sanskrit: yena sūdayase śatrūn samare sūryavarcasā vajro vajradharasyeva so 'yaṃ te satatārcitaḥ
english: This bow of yours, with which you used to destroy enemies in battle, shining like the sun — like the thunderbolt of the thunderbolt-wielder — this ever-honored weapon of yours —

sanskrit: raṇe śatrupraharaṇo hemajālapariṣkṛtaḥ parigho vyavakīrṇas te bāṇaiś chinnaḥ sahasradhā
english: — your iron club, which struck enemies in battle, adorned with networks of gold, lies scattered, cut by arrows into a thousand pieces.

sanskrit: dhig astu hṛdayaṃ yasyā mamedaṃ na sahasradhā tvayi pañcatvam āpanne phalate śokapīḍitam
english: Shame upon this heart of mine that it does not burst into a thousand pieces — tormented with grief as it is — now that you have attained the five elements.

sanskrit: etasminn antare rāmo vibhīṣaṇam uvāca ha saṃskāraḥ kriyatāṃ bhrātuḥ striyaś caitā nivartaya
english: At this juncture Rāma said to Vibhīṣaṇa: 'Let the funeral rites be performed for your brother, and turn back these women.'

sanskrit: taṃ praśritas tato rāmaṃ śrutavākyo vibhīṣaṇaḥ vimṛśya buddhyā dharmajño dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ rāmasyaivānuvṛttyartham uttaraṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Then Vibhīṣaṇa, humbly hearing those words, the knower of righteousness, having deliberated with his mind on a reply consistent with both dharma and purpose, spoke in deference to Rāma.

sanskrit: tyaktadharmavrataṃ krūraṃ nṛśaṃsam anṛtaṃ tathā nāham arho 'smi saṃskartuṃ paradārābhimarśakam
english: 'I am not fit to perform the rites for one who abandoned the vow of righteousness, who is cruel, brutal, false, and who violated another man's wife.'

sanskrit: bhrātṛrūpo hi me śatrur eṣa sarvāhite rataḥ rāvaṇo nārhate pūjāṃ pūjyo 'pi gurugauravāt
english: 'This Rāvaṇa, who took the form of a brother, was ever devoted to universal harm; he does not deserve honor, though he might be honored on account of reverence due to an elder.'

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsa iti māṃ rāma vakṣyanti manujā bhuvi śrutvā tasya guṇān sarve vakṣyanti sukṛtaṃ punaḥ
english: 'O Rāma, people on earth will call me cruel; but all, hearing of his qualities, will speak of his good deeds again.'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā paramaprīto rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ vibhīṣaṇam uvācedaṃ vākyajño vākyakovidam
english: Hearing that, Rāma, foremost among those who uphold righteousness, supremely pleased, spoke thus to Vibhīṣaṇa who was skilled in speech and an expert in counsel.

sanskrit: tavāpi me priyaṃ kāryaṃ tvatprabhavāc ca me jitam avaśyaṃ tu kṣamaṃ vācyo mayā tvaṃ rākṣaseśvara
english: 'What is dear to you is what I must do, and through you this conquest has been mine; yet, O lord of rākṣasas, I must necessarily say something fitting to you.'

sanskrit: adharmānṛtasaṃyuktaḥ kāmam eṣa niśācaraḥ tejasvī balavāñ śūraḥ saṃgrāmeṣu ca nityaśaḥ
english: 'Though this night-rover was joined with unrighteousness and falsehood, he was nonetheless glorious, strong, brave, and ever so in battles.

sanskrit: śatakratumukhair devaiḥ śrūyate na parājitaḥ mahātmā balasaṃpanno rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ
english: 'The great-souled Rāvaṇa, cause of lament to the world, endowed with strength — it is heard that he was not defeated even by gods led by the Hundred-Sacrificed Indra.

sanskrit: maraṇāntāni vairāṇi nirvṛttaṃ naḥ prayojanam kriyatām asya saṃskāro mamāpy eṣa yathā tava
english: 'Enmities end with death; our purpose is accomplished. Let his funeral rites be performed — he is as much mine as yours.'

sanskrit: tvatsakāśān mahābāho saṃskāraṃ vidhipūrvakam kṣipram arhati dharmajña tvaṃ yaśobhāg bhaviṣyasi
english: 'O mighty-armed, O knower of dharma, he deserves a proper funeral rite to be performed quickly by you; you will thereby become a sharer of glory.'

sanskrit: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā tvaramāṇo vibhīṣaṇaḥ saṃskāreṇānurūpeṇa yojayām āsa rāvaṇam
english: Hearing Rāghava's words, Vibhīṣaṇa, hastening, provided Rāvaṇa with the fitting funeral rite.

sanskrit: sa dadau pāvakaṃ tasya vidhiyuktaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ tāḥ striyo 'nunayām āsa sāntvam uktvā punaḥ punaḥ
english: Vibhīṣaṇa offered the sacred fire to him according to the prescribed rite, and consoled those women, speaking words of comfort again and again.

sanskrit: praviṣṭāsu ca sarvāsu rākṣasīṣu vibhīṣaṇaḥ rāmapārśvam upāgamya tadātiṣṭhad vinītavat
english: When all the rākṣasī women had gone back inside, Vibhīṣaṇa came to Rāma's side and stood there in a humble manner.

sanskrit: rāmo 'pi saha sainyena sasugrīvaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ harṣaṃ lebhe ripuṃ hatvā yathā vṛtraṃ śatakratuḥ
english: And Rāma too, together with his army, with Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa, attained joy at having slain his enemy, as the Hundred-Sacrificed Indra had upon slaying Vṛtra.
